target_customer: E-commerce brands, first-time product entrepreneurs and later Fortune 500 buyers who manufacture products in Asia
problem: Small brands could not find or vet overseas factories, and factories rarely talk directly to customers.
business_model: Fee plus commission: $500 fee and 1 to 10 percent of order cost in 2018; later managed manufacturing and sourcing services

founders.name: Nathan Resnick
previous_startups: Described as on his third startup (Times of San Diego, via search)
founders.background_notes: Education and later role changes appear only in aggregator profiles and are not recorded.

competitors.name: Alibaba
competitors.what: Marketplace where buyers find Chinese factories and talk to sales reps
competitors.traction_then: Default channel for overseas sourcing, per the TechCrunch description of the status quo

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching and project-management workflow; the hard part was the factory network and vetting, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Vetted factory relationships help but other sourcing agents and marketplaces can copy the model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent is reported to have acquired or copied it in sources found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Feb 2018) reported a 92 percent conversion after order submission, average order about 30,000 dollars and about 100 product categories.

brand_strength.rationale: No sourced press about the brand; the name is shared with an Ethereum code-verification project, which crowds search.

pivots.from: Self-serve style factory matching with order fee
pivots.to: Managed manufacturing and fractional sourcing services
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from homepage services versus the 2018 model, so undated

outcome_analysis: Sourcify stayed small and says it is profitable, with a 2018 model of 500 dollar fees plus commission and a current offer of managed manufacturing across local teams in 17 countries. Funding is poorly documented; aggregators list only a small amount, so growth appears to have been capital efficient rather than venture-scale.
notes: Funding: aggregators (CB Insights) list about 120K over six rounds including a 2018 seed and May 2019 angel, unverified, no round recorded. No acquisition, layoff or shutdown news found. Competitors: only Alibaba appears in a 2018 source; Xometry, Fictiv and 3D Hubs address custom parts and were not named by Sourcify sources, so not listed. Me.sh profile claims Resnick moved to board in November 2022; unverified.
